title: Predictive micro-scaling, warm-standby, and isolation-tagging — PRD (wip)
body:
Status: draft — brainstorming + early design.

Summary:
We propose a predictive micro-scaling feature that provides low-latency capacity for bursty tenants by combining: (1) fine-grained (per-tenant, per-model) micro-scaling windows, (2) warm-standby snapshots (lightweight runtime state + KV cache prefetch), and (3) an isolation-tagging system that maps tenant workload fingerprints to soft isolation lanes. The goal is to reduce cold-start latency for short-lived spikes while preserving Dedicated capacity predictability and tenant isolation guarantees.

Problem statement (why this?):
- Many tenants experience short micro-bursts (seconds to a few minutes) that are expensive to cover with full reserved capacity.
- Current Dedicated burst options either allocate coarse-grained burst credits or rely on broad autoscale ramps that introduce latency or eviction risk for other tenants.
- Cold starts for model states / KV caches add tens-to-hundreds of ms for bursty requests, degrading UX for real-time features.
- Need a way to handle micro-spikes while maintaining tenant fairness and SLOs.

Goals:
- Serve micro-bursts with tail latency within existing SLO bands (e.g., p95/p99 targets) without requiring customers to reserve large capacity windows.
- Offer predictable billing semantics for micro-surge handling (metering + optional credit consumption).
- Keep isolation guarantees: noisy tenant spikes must not materially worsen other tenants' latency or cause excessive preemption.
- Provide observability and tuning knobs (per-tenant warm-standby budgets, fingerprinting sensitivity).

Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for long-running reserved capacity. Tenants with sustained high throughput should use Dedicated reservations.
- Not intended for multi-tenant noisy-neighbor mitigation at hardware level (that is separate SRE/infra layer).

Key concepts / definitions:
- Micro-window: a short timeslice (configurable, default 30s) during which the platform can attach transient micro-workers to handle bursts.
- Warm-standby snapshot: a lightweight prewarmed runtime bundle that includes model weights loaded in fast path (quantized variant if relevant), warmed KV cache prefixes, and ephemeral routing state. Snapshots are small-lived and evictable.
- Isolation-tag (iso-tag): metadata assigned to tenant+model that indicates which soft isolation lane the tenant prefers or requires (e.g., high-isolation, best-effort, latency-priority). Iso-tags influence co-location decisions and prewarm placement.
- Predictive signal: short-horizon forecast (10s–2min) derived from traffic patterns, rate-of-change heuristics, and optional customer hints (scheduled promotions) used to preemptively create warm-standby snapshots.

High-level proposal:
1) Admission & prediction pipeline
  - Ingest request rate/time-series per-tenant/model. Compute a short-horizon derivative and synthetic features (recent slope, intra-minute percentiles, request-coalescing patterns).
  - Apply lightweight predictor (rules + exponential smoothing; ML model optionally in later phase) to estimate probability of a micro-burst in next micro-window.
  - If probability > threshold and tenant has budget/permissions, schedule warm-standby for the micro-window.

2) Warm-standby lifecycle
  - Create snapshot on selected node(s) with: model loaded, tokenization warmed, short prefix cache seeded (based on last N requests or synthetic top-K prefixes), and a warmed execution context.
  - Snapshots are tagged with iso-tag and a tenant micro-window reservation id. They expire after micro-window or earlier if unused.
  - Charging: small per-snapshot standby fee + per-token if used. Optionally consume tenant burst credits.

3) Micro-scaling attach/detach
  - When burst arrives, route requests to micro-workers attached to snapshots. Micro-workers run on isolated execution contexts with rate-limits bound to micro-window.
  - If micro-workers exceed a local threshold, fall back to either: (a) degrade fidelity (model variant/quantization), (b) enqueue with latency-aware queueing, or (c) spill to a lower-isolation lane (respecting tenant policy).

4) Isolation-tagging and placement
  - Iso-tagging is customer-configurable on route/tenant level. Default auto-tagging uses tenant history (latency sensitivity heuristics).
  - Scheduler places snapshots preferentially co-located with similar iso-tagged tenants only when lane headroom exists. High-isolation tags restrict co-location aggressively.
  - Soft-eviction rules ensure snapshots are the first to free to restore core reserved capacity. If eviction required, platform notifies tenant via events.

Telemetry and SLOs:
- New telemetry streams: micro-window creation/eviction events, snapshot attach latencies, snapshot hit-rate (served from warm-standby vs cold path), micro-window tail latencies p50/p95/p99, and prewarm false-positive rate.
- SLOs: maintain p95 within X ms of baseline for micro-window-attached requests; p99 must not regress more than Y% for co-located tenants. (Exact X/Y to be calibrated in experiment.)

Customer UX / API surface:
- New route flags: micro_scaling: {enabled: bool, budget: tokens|credits, iso_tag: string, sensitivity: low|med|high}
- Admin console: timeline UI showing scheduled micro-windows, snapshot inventory, and per-route micro-billing.
- Alerts: when warm-standby triggered, when preempted, and if predictive model high false-positive.

Billing model (initial suggestion):
- Standby reservation fee: small per-minute per-snapshot charge (to cover memory residency).
- Usage billing: normal per-token bill when requests served. If snapshot is prewarmed proactively on tenant hint (customer-initiated schedule), optional discounted standby fee.
- Burst credit consumption: tenants with burst credits can opt to draw down credits to accelerate/guarantee warm-standby. Credits are consumed on attach; snapshot creation alone can have a smaller credit deduction.

Operational considerations / infra constraints:
- Snapshot memory budget must be tightly limited (tiny stacks). Prefer quantized models for snapshot path.
- Scheduler must be fast (<50ms decision) to avoid adding latency during attach. Maintain per-node snapshot index for O(1) placement.
- Eviction policy: LRU with iso-tag weight adjustments; prefer evicting best-effort snapshots first.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiments): implement prediction rules and prototype snapshot creation on small internal cluster. Run synthetic replay (RED-4213) to validate attach latencies and false-positive costs.
- Phase 1 (beta): enable for internal / opt-in customers. Expose simple flags and billing. Collect telemetry for SLO calibrations.
- Phase 2 (GA): wider release with ML-based predictor, richer console controls, and SLA addendum for premium tenants.

Milestones & rough timeline (quarterly plan):
- Q1: rules predictor + snapshot prototype + simulator + initial telemetry hooks (2 engineers, 1 SRE).
- Q2: placement/iso-tagging integration + cost model + billing stub + internal beta.
- Q3: customer beta + ML predictor + console UX polish + security review.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: false-positive prewarms increase cost. Mitigate: conservative thresholds, cooldown windows, and backoff on repeated misses.
- Risk: warm-standbys reduce core pool headroom, causing SLO regressions for reserved tenants. Mitigate: strict hard caps, configurable tenant budgets, immediate eviction priority.
- Risk: complexity in billing confuses customers. Mitigate: clear default (opt-out) and transparent invoice line-items plus simulation tool.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Quantitative thresholds: target micro-window length, snapshot mem budget per model, and standby fee. Need simulator runs. (TODO: run RED-4378 workload traces).
- Policy for multi-model routes (how many snapshots to create for same tenant if they call multiple models?).
- Should snapshots support partial KV only (prefixes) vs full KV warm? Tradeoffs on memory and hit-rate.
- Integrate with Dedicated autoscaler: how to treat micro-workers in node utilization calculations? (avoid autoscaler thrash).

Appendix — simulation notes (quick):
- Ran a 24h replay of three customers (ecommerce push, chat assistant, QA tool) with engineered microbursts. Conservative rule predictor captured ~65% of bursts with <0.2 snapshot-minutes per predicted burst (prelim). Need more runs across region topology.

Notes to product/engineers:
- Keep the first iteration rule-based and observable; avoid adding ML until we have clean telemetry.
- Emphasize billing transparency in beta. Customers hate surprises.
- For prototypes, favor lightweight snapshot contents: tokenizer + top-K prefix cache + light model mapping (no full weight reload on snapshot if avoidable).

Contact / owners: Maya Gonzalez (product lead) — maya@redwood.ai; engineering counterparts: Omar Li (platform), Priya Desai (runtime), Connor Blake (infra).

End of draft.
